title: Given a Scenario, Install and Configure Cloud-Based Productivity Tools

sections.title: What You Are Learning
paragraphs: Cloud productivity environments provide communication, applications, identity, and data through connected services rather than relying only on local software.
The main mental model is: identity → license → applications → storage → sync → collaborate.
bullets: Spreadsheets, videoconferencing, presentation, word processing, and instant messaging

sections.title: Maestro Focus
paragraphs: When setting up a user with cloud productivity services, can you determine whether the requirement involves email, storage, synchronization, collaboration, identity, or licensing?
bullets: Keep local and cloud folders aligned → sync settings
Accounts aligned across systems → identity synchronization

sections.title: Cloud-Based Productivity
paragraphs: Cloud productivity tools let users access applications, files, and communication services from multiple devices while supporting collaboration, synchronization, centralized administration, and remote work.
sections.callout: User plus cloud identity and license → productivity services.

sections.title: Email Systems
paragraphs: A cloud email system centrally hosts mailboxes that users access through web interfaces, desktop clients, or mobile applications. Setup may involve the user account, mailbox, authentication, client synchronization, organizational configuration, and licensing.
sections.callout: A user can sign in but has no mailbox functionality → verify email-service configuration and licensing.

sections.title: Storage
paragraphs: Cloud storage keeps files on provider-hosted infrastructure so authorized users can upload, download, share, access, and collaborate across devices.
sections.callout: Storage describes where cloud data resides.

sections.title: Sync/Folder Settings
paragraphs: Synchronization keeps selected local and cloud copies aligned in both directions. Verify the signed-in account, sync status, selected folders, and whether local copies are retained.
sections.callout: Files appear online but not in the expected desktop folder → check sync/folder settings.

sections.title: Collaboration Tools
paragraphs: Cloud collaboration lets multiple users share, comment on, co-edit, and review content without occupying the same physical location.

entries.title: Spreadsheets
paragraphs: Organize data into rows and columns and support formulas, calculations, charts, and collaborative editing.
entries.recognitionCue: A team needs shared budget calculations → spreadsheet.

entries.title: Videoconferencing
paragraphs: Provides real-time audio, video, online meetings, and screen sharing.

entries.title: Presentation Tools
paragraphs: Create slide-based visual presentations.
entries.recognitionCue: Build a slide deck → presentation tool.

entries.title: Word Processing Tools
paragraphs: Create and edit reports, letters, documentation, and other text-oriented documents, often collaboratively.
entries.recognitionCue: Create a written report → word processing.

entries.title: Instant Messaging
paragraphs: Provides near-real-time direct or group text communication, presence, and often file sharing.

table.caption: Match the task to the tool

sections.title: Identity Synchronization
paragraphs: Identity synchronization keeps user and account information aligned between connected identity environments. Missing or incorrect synchronization can cause missing cloud accounts, sign-in failures, bad account data, and access problems.
sections.callout: Who you are → identity sync. What you saved → file sync.

sections.title: Licensing Assignment
paragraphs: Cloud productivity services commonly use per-user or subscription licensing. A valid account can authenticate successfully yet lack a mailbox, application, storage allocation, or collaboration feature until the correct license is assigned.

table.caption: Identity and licensing
rows: Which paid or authorized services may the user use?

sections.callout: Login succeeds but the application reports no entitlement → check licensing assignment.

sections.title: Cloud Productivity Setup Workflow
bullets: Establish that the user can authenticate.
Confirm identity synchronization created or aligned the correct cloud account.
Configure the email mailbox and client access.
Configure the correct sync folders and verify sync status.
Confirm access to word processing, spreadsheets, presentations, videoconferencing, and messaging.

entries.title: Authenticated but Services Are Missing
paragraphs: If a new employee signs in successfully but email, storage, or videoconferencing is unavailable, first verify that the required services and licenses were assigned.

entries.title: Files Differ Across Devices
paragraphs: If identity and the application work but an edited file does not appear elsewhere, verify the correct account, selected folders, current sync status, and network access.

entries.title: Cloud Storage Is Not Automatically Backup
paragraphs: Synchronization copies changes—including deletions or unwanted edits—to connected locations. A backup strategy preserves recoverable versions independently of normal sync behavior.

sections.title: Recognition Cues
bullets: Local and cloud folders differ → sync settings
Accounts aligned across systems → identity synchronization
Valid user lacks application entitlement → licensing assignment

entries.title: Storage vs. Synchronization
paragraphs: Storage is where cloud data resides; synchronization keeps local and cloud copies aligned.

entries.title: Identity Sync vs. File Sync
paragraphs: Identity sync aligns accounts; file sync aligns documents and data.

entries.title: Authentication vs. Licensing
paragraphs: If the user cannot sign in, investigate identity and authentication. If sign-in succeeds but a service is unavailable, licensing is a strong suspect.

entries.title: Email vs. Instant Messaging
paragraphs: Email is a mailbox system; instant messaging is real-time chat.

entries.title: Videoconferencing vs. Presentation
paragraphs: Videoconferencing is a live meeting; a presentation tool creates a slide deck.

entries.title: Synchronization vs. Backup
paragraphs: Sync keeps copies aligned; backup preserves recoverable copies. Sync is not automatically backup.

sections.title: Maestro Recognition Sheet
bullets: Accounts aligned between systems → identity synchronization
Signs in but lacks service → licensing
